description: Discovery hypothesis: small subcontractors on DBRA-covered projects may struggle to assemble job-specific hours, classifications, wages and fringe-benefit data for weekly payroll certification. The recurring task is documented; unmet small-business pain is not yet established.
customer_segment: Hypothesized segment: US small construction subcontractors on covered federal or federally assisted projects; source does not isolate firm size.
geography: United States; only applicable covered contracts, not all construction payroll.
context: Payroll administrator or owner prepares weekly reporting and compliance certification. No employer records were accessed.

evidence.text: DOL states that covered contractors and subcontractors must submit payroll information weekly with a signed Statement of Compliance.
The instructions distinguish labor classifications and fringe-benefit treatment, creating multiple inputs to the reporting task.
DOL estimates an average of 55 minutes to complete the information collection, including review and data gathering; this is not a measured small-business time saving and is not extrapolated.
Sunburst describes additional employee/job/wage/deduction data stored in linked records and merged with QuickBooks data. This establishes configuration, not that users suffer unresolved re-entry.

alternatives: LCPcertified: advertised payroll upload, validation and certified-report/XML generation.
Sunburst CPS: advertised QuickBooks Desktop integration plus linked-record setup and paper/electronic reporting.
Payroll4Construction: advertised managed payroll from submitted timecards, QuickBooks accounting integration and automatic certified reports.

contradictory_evidence.text: WH-347 is optional: a proposed product cannot assume every contractor must re-enter data into this exact form.
DOL identifies limited DBRA coverage and injunction-affected provisions; not every construction firm or activity belongs in this segment.
Three suppliers already advertise certified-report workflows, so a generic report-generation product would duplicate existing alternatives rather than establish differentiation.
Sunburst explicitly excludes QBO, but this is a single vendor limitation, not evidence that no QBO-compatible alternative exists.

uncertainty: Recurring reporting is supported. Manual duplication, avoidable hours, current software gaps, buyer access, error costs and willingness to pay are unknown. A single agency burden estimate is not customer validation. Issue #6 found advertised alternatives but no independently verified residual exception workload. Current interoperability, source-stack fit, switching friction and a QBO-specific gap remain unknown.
open_questions: After selecting one source payroll stack and one destination portal, what specific required fields still need recurring manual transformation?
Do those exceptions persist after correct incumbent setup, and how often do small subcontractors encounter them?
Which current QBO-compatible solutions already serve this exact workflow?
next_actions: Narrow any continued desk research to one payroll-stack/destination pair; obtain current official import/export field documentation.
Seek dated first-hand contractor evidence before escalating to an opportunity. Pause generic WH-347 automation work absent a differentiated gap.
title: Weekly certified payroll preparation for covered construction subcontractors

history.reason: Initial public-source discovery for issue #4; no customer interviews or commercial validation.
Issue #6: added three-vendor comparison and integration-boundary evidence; narrowed the generic automation thesis without changing the original documented reporting obligation.
